title: Background tasks and refresh: what iOS actually allows

videos.script: Close an app on an iPhone, and within seconds it stops. Not slows down. Stops. {{suspend}} It stays in memory, using nothing, until the system needs the room. {{ask}} Anything it does later, it does because the system gives it time. And the system gives that time on its own terms. {{refresh}} Today the planner asks for a refresh. It declares it in Info.plist, it submits a request, and it attaches the work to its scene. Up to thirty seconds, when the system chooses. {{when}} Then the two decisions the app does make. When to ask: in fifteen minutes if sessions are waiting, otherwise at six in the morning. You will see a calendar get one night right that adding hours gets wrong. {{cut}} And what to do when the time runs out. The system cancels the task. So the work saves after every session it sends. {{linux}} Cancelling is ordinary Swift, so you practise the whole expiration on your own machine. One second at a time, two sessions at a time, and nothing lost.
